name: DECLARE
author: István Koren
description: Declarative process mining: instead of a model you can walk through, a list of rules the process never broke — “every claim is eventually assessed”, “payment only happens after approval”, “these two never both occur”. This is the paradigm for flexible processes, where the imperative model is a spaghetti diagram that allows almost everything and explains nothing. Discovers a DECLARE model from a log, and checks any DECLARE model against any log, naming the cases that broke each rule.

actions.label: Discover DECLARE model
actions.description: Measures every candidate rule over the log's activities — eighteen templates over every ordered pair — and keeps the ones that hold often enough and were put to the test often enough. Support is how often a rule held; confidence is how often it held when it could have been broken, so a rule about something that almost never happens cannot coast on an empty truth. Redundant rules are removed: if the log obeys “A is always immediately followed by B” there is no point also reporting “A is eventually followed by B”.

agent.whenToUse: For a flexible process whose imperative model is unreadable, or to state what a log always does without committing to an order of work.
agent.notFor: Replaying or simulating. A DECLARE model constrains behaviour rather than generating it, so there is no play-out and no token game.
examples: minSupport 1 for the rules that were never once broken
minConfidence 0.9 with minSupport 0.5 for rules that hold whenever they apply, even if they rarely apply
negative false to leave out the “these two never both happen” family

minSupport.title: Minimum support
minSupport.description: Keep a rule only if it holds in at least this share of cases. 1 means it was never broken.

minConfidence.title: Minimum confidence
minConfidence.description: Keep a rule only if it held in at least this share of the cases that could have broken it. This is what separates a rule from a truth nobody ever tested: a rule that is never activated scores zero here however high its support.

prune.title: Remove redundant rules
prune.description: Drop a rule that a stronger rule already implies — “A is eventually followed by B” when the log says “A is immediately followed by B”. What is dropped is counted, never silently lost.

unary.title: Rules about single activities
unary.description: Existence, absence, exactly once, starts with, ends with.

relations.title: Ordering rules
relations.description: Responded existence, response, precedence and succession — “eventually”, at any distance.

alternating.title: Alternating rules
alternating.description: The same orderings, but with nothing of the same kind in between: A, B, A, B rather than A, A, B.

chain.title: Immediate rules
chain.description: Chain response, precedence and succession — one activity directly after the other, with nothing at all in between.

negative.title: Rules about what never happens
negative.description: Not co-existence, not succession, not chain succession. These are often the most interesting rules a log has, and the ones an imperative model cannot state at all.

limit.title: Most rules to keep
limit.description: A cap on the model's size, applied after ranking by confidence. A model larger than this is a list, not a description; what was cut is reported.

maxActivities.title: Activity limit
maxActivities.description: Keeps only the most frequent activities. Every ordered pair is a candidate rule, so the work grows with the square of this — and so does the model.

actions.label: Check DECLARE rules
actions.description: Checks a DECLARE model against a log, case by case: which rules were broken, how often, and by which cases. A declarative model makes this simpler than alignment does — there is no search and no cost, only a rule and the cases that broke it. Rules the log never activates are reported separately, because a model that says nothing about a log is a different finding from a model it obeys.

agent.whenToUse: To test a model discovered from one log (or written by hand) against another period, another site, or the cases you suspect.
agent.notFor: Measuring fitness of an imperative model — use conformance checking (alignments) for a Petri net.

maxCases.title: Cases to list
maxCases.description: How many violating cases to name, worst first. The counts are over the whole log whatever this is set to; this only bounds the list.

maxActivities.title: Activity limit
maxActivities.description: Keeps only the most frequent activities. A rule about an activity outside the limit is reported as naming an activity this log does not record, rather than silently passing.

authors.name: István Koren
authors.affiliation: ELTE University Budapest, Data Science and Engineering

citation.text: Pesic, M., Schonenberg, H. and van der Aalst, W.M.P. (2007). DECLARE: Full Support for Loosely-Structured Processes. EDOC 2007, 287-298. Discovery follows Maggi, F.M., Bose, R.P.J.C. and van der Aalst, W.M.P. (2012), Efficient Discovery of Understandable Declarative Process Models from Event Logs, CAiSE 2012, LNCS 7328, 270-285.
